title: Online frontier-point /apply full-clears quote_grid/solver, ending the frontier session and breaking a subsequent apply of a different point
description: In apply_lambdas, the frontier-point branch (target_point_index is not None) calls _store.clear_result_data(body.job_id) with no keys argument, which defaults to the full _HEAVY_OBJECT_KEYS set = ('solver','solve_result','quote_grid','factors_df','ratebook_factor_contexts'). This wipes quote_grid and solver even though the user is mid frontier-analysis (they just applied a specific frontier point). Every OTHER frontier-session exit in this module deliberately preserves that heavy state: the non-frontier apply branch (line 1330) and the save/mlflow paths use _clear_result_data_after_user_action, which keeps quote_grid/solver when the job still has frontier points and only strips solve_result; and the ratebook frontier-select/apply paths (lines 1485, 1507) clear only ('solve_result',). The helper _clear_result_data_after_user_action exists precisely for this: its docstring says 'Slim result data without ending an active frontier-analysis session' (line 664), and _job_has_frontier_points gates retention. Consequence: after applying online frontier point 0, applying a DIFFERENT point N (which has no cached frontier_apply_result:N artifact) re-enters _materialise_frontier_point_apply and hits _store.touch_heavy_objects(job_id, required_keys=('quote_grid',)) at line 1025, which now returns False because quote_grid was cleared, raising HTTP 400 'Quote grid is not available for this job. Re-run the solve to materialise this frontier point.' (lines 1026-1042). The online apply path even persists per-point artifacts and carries its own re-run-the-solve copy, signalling an intended multi-point session, yet it self-destructs the runtime state needed for it after the first apply.
evidence: apply_lambdas line 1288: `_store.clear_result_data(body.job_id)` (full clear) vs the non-frontier branch line 1330 `_clear_result_data_after_user_action(body.job_id)`. clear_result_data default keys = _HEAVY_OBJECT_KEYS (optimiser.py imports / _job_store.py:30-31,508-511 includes 'quote_grid'). _clear_result_data_after_user_action (optimiser.py:663-670) retains heavy state when _job_has_frontier_points(job) is True, clearing only solve_result. Re-apply trace: _materialise_frontier_point_apply (online) line 1025 `if not _store.touch_heavy_objects(job_id, required_keys=('quote_grid',)): raise HTTPException(400, ...)` — touch_heavy_objects returns False when quote_grid is absent (_job_store.py:320-321). The intended-symmetry contract is pinned for ratebook by tests/test_optimiser_routes.py:9780-9858 (test_apply_ratebook_frontier_point_rejection_preserves_rate_table_switching), which asserts job['solver'], job['quote_grid'], job['ratebook_factor_contexts'] all survive an apply within a frontier session so other points can still be materialised; no test asserts the online path SHOULD full-clear quote_grid (the only online apply-then-state test, lines 8902-9005, applies a single point and re-creates frontier state).
